items.title: The top 5 analyst questions from CVS Health’s Q3 2026 earnings call
items.summary: CVS Health’s latest quarter saw the company deliver revenue and profit above Wall Street’s expectations, but the market responded negatively. Management pointed to consistent gains in its core segments, driven by pharmacy strength and progress in Medicare margin recovery. CEO David Joyner highlighted the quarter as "another demonstration of disciplined execution," emphasizing ongoing improvement in the company’s medical benefit ratio and strong cash flow generation.

items.title: Medicare Just Locked In Most of Your 2027 Costs. One Big Number Is Still Missing
items.summary: Medicare open enrollment ends Dec. 7, and most 2027 costs are set: a $2,400 Part D cap, a $700 deductible and a 3.6% COLA. For a 72-year-old with one costly drug, the bill rises $300, her check nets about $76 more a month, and a plan comparison is worth $408.

items.title: CVS Health (CVS) Challenges Tennessee PBM Ownership Ban In Federal Court
items.summary: CVS Health (NYSE:CVS) has filed a federal lawsuit contesting Tennessee's new law that blocks pharmacies from owning pharmacy benefit managers. The legal action follows CVS Health's previously announced plan to separate into two companies that would split its pharmacy and PBM operations. CVS Health has stated that pharmacy services for Tennessee patients will continue without interruption while the dispute proceeds. items.title: CVS Health (CVS) Stock Could Be Cheap On Earnings Alone
items.summary: CVS Health has delivered a solid share price gain over the past few years, yet the stock has recently pulled back and is now heading into a major breakup of the business. This puts fresh focus on whether the current price makes sense relative to its earnings power. With the shares closing at US$83.85, investors are asking if the recent news and the longer term performance leave the earnings story fully reflected in the valuation or not.
